summary: A fire lookout since 1921 whose 82-foot L-4 tower dates from 1949; no longer used for detection and now posted closed.

facts.design: 82-foot open timber tower with an L-4 cab (added 1950)
facts.status_note: Still standing but listed as abandoned and posted to stay off.

staffing.status: Not staffed; a 1987 Forest Service statement says it is no longer used for fire detection, and a 2023 visitor found it unstaffed.

access.note: The tower is closed and posted to stay off. A 2020 account lists the site as drive-up; a 2023 visitor reached the lookout on foot via the Sugarloaf Trail.

visit.climbable: not stated in the sources; posted to stay off
visit.trail_note: Sugarloaf Trail: 1.9 miles from the trailhead to the lookout access road, then 0.2 miles to the lookout (2023 visit).

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Wallowa-Whitman National Forest

events.note: Fire detection site with a 50-foot pole tower and open cab.
A diary extract records lightning starting six fires while the lookout was at the tower.
Forest Lookouts dates an 82-foot treated timber tower to 1941; the 1949 newspaper items and other sources date it to 1949.
Present 82-foot tower constructed; newspapers in August to October 1949 report work under way.
L-4 cab added to the top of the tower.
Time-lapse motion picture camera to be installed at the lookout to record how lightning storms build up (July 28, 1954 item).
David Wirth stationed at the lookout for the fire season.
Doug Payton stationed at the lookout.
Forest Service says the lookout is no longer used for fire detection and asks the public for ideas on its future.
Firelookout.com says the tower was threatened by a forest fire in the 1990s; no exact year given.

corrections.why: NHLR and firelookout.com give the tower standing today as 82 feet (about 25.0 m). 15.2 m is 50 feet, the height of the earlier 1921 pole tower, not the current tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts also lists an 82-foot tower erected in 1941. The 1949 newspaper items, NHLR, firelookout.com and the 2023 visit date the current tower to 1949. Story uses 1949.
A 1949 newspaper gives 80 feet; NHLR, firelookout.com and the 1950 newspaper give 82 feet. Story uses 82.

Firelookout.com (undated) says the tower is available for emergencies. The 1987 Forest Service statement and the 2023 visit say it is no longer used for detection and is abandoned. Story follows the later accounts.

sources.title: Russel Mountain – Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 15.2 is the 1921 pole tower (50 ft), corrected to 25.0 m for the 82-foot tower. Access is marked closed for the tower; the road and trailhead are described as open in 2020 and 2023 accounts, but no official Forest Service notice was read. The 1941 Forest Lookouts date conflicts with 1949 sources. A Twin Lakes fire near-miss item seen in search results was not fetched and is not used. Staffing after 1964 not found. Newest status evidence is the 2023 visit.
